subject: Solstice - Sudden tail-latency increase affecting hosted API (investigation & mitigation)
messages:
From: Maya Patterson <maya@solstice.ai>

Cc: platform@solstice.ai
Date: 2028-03-12T08:15:00Z
Subject: Re: degradation - p95/p99 spike starting 03/11 22:00 UTC

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a sudden jump in p95/p99 latency and a small uptick in 500s across our integration starting last night (~22:00 UTC). The UX for our customers is degraded — some requests take multiple seconds longer and a small percentage fail outright.

Quick details:
- Region: us-east-1 (hosted API)
- Started: 2028-03-11 22:00 UTC
- Symptom: p95 doubled, p99 tripled for generation endpoints; error rate +1.9% vs baseline
- Attached: example-payload.json (one failing request body)
- We are on the Redwood hosted plan, no recent config changes on our end.

Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side and provide an ETA for mitigation? We need to decide whether to failover traffic elsewhere. This is impacting a portion of our paid customers.

Thanks —
Maya

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-12T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: degradation - initial infra notes

Quick summary from infra triage (initial, exploratory):

What I see:
- Starting ~03/11 21:50 UTC there was a multi-tenant pattern where Solstice's request size distribution shifted (median seq len +30%, tail much heavier).
- That increased the effective batch processing time and caused continuous batching windows to grow. Queue depth for Solstice's shards rose ~3x, which drove scheduling contention and KV-cache churn in the serving runtime.
- Result: tail latency amplification (p95/p99) and a small increase in transient 500s when batches timed out.

Potential root contributors:
- Batch-window backpressure heuristic didn't adapt quickly to the sudden seq-length distribution shift.
- Per-tenant routing puts Solstice on a set of smaller instances with less KV capacity; when load spiked, we saw cache eviction/rehydration thrash.

Immediate mitigations I'm proposing (can be applied within minutes):
1) Reduce global batch window from 12ms -> 6ms for Solstice's shard (early flush) to prevent long batch waits.
2) Enable per-tenant early-flush for long-sequence requests.
3) Temporarily move Solstice traffic to a larger-instance pool (w/ bigger KV capacity) while we stabilize.
4) Purge stale KV entries for Solstice to avoid repeated rehabs.

I've attached a short snapshot of the runtime stacks and queue metrics: stack-snap.txt.

I'll start applying (1) and (2) now and report back in 15 min. If that reduces queue depth we'll avoid full migration.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Attachment: stack-snap.txt (text)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-12T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: mitigation options / temporary controls

Following Marcus's note — SRE actions and risk assessment: 

Actions we can take in the next 30–60 minutes:
- Apply per-tenant redirection to larger-instance pool (low-risk, small ramp).
- Add conservative per-API-route rate limiting (soft headroom) for non-essential calls (retries/backfills) to reduce noise.
- Enable temporary fallback to smaller-model-variant for streaming-heavy endpoints (slightly lower quality, much lower token compute).

Risks:
- Rate-limiting will impact some throughput and could surface to customers as throttled requests.
- Moving to larger instances will briefly shift latency distribution as connections warm; expected net improvement for tail.

I'm ready to push the redirection and the early-flush config. Recommend we: 1) enable early-flush and soft rate-limits now, 2) if p99 still elevated after 15–20m, start redirection.

Note: HubSpot incident: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/98765

—Aditya

Hi Maya —

Thanks for flagging this. Quick update from our side and proposed next steps: 

What we're doing now:
- We've enabled an early-flush batch window for your shard and applied a conservative rate-limit for non-critical endpoints.
- SRE is standing by to move traffic to a larger-instance pool if tail latency does not improve within the next 20 minutes.

What we request from you:
- If acceptable, allow us to enable a temporary fallback model variant for streaming endpoints for up to 2 hours (this reduces compute per-token and should improve p99).

Compensation and SLA note:
- We'll issue a credit for the impacted window if our mitigation does not restore agreed latency SLOs. We will also provide an executive summary once triage completes.

I'll post a 15-minute cadence update here. Apologies for the disruption — we're prioritizing Solstice.

Best,

Laura —

I'm escalating this to you for exec visibility and approval on a short customer credit. Solstice (Solstice AI) is experiencing a p95/p99 regression tied to batching and queue depth for their hosted shard. Timeline and current state below: 

Timeline:
- 2028-03-11 21:50 UTC: Solstice request distribution shifted (tailier sequences)
- 2028-03-12 08:15 UTC: Solstice filed ticket — initial customer report (see thread)
- 2028-03-12 09:00 UTC: Infra applied early-flush batch windows and cache purge; observed partial improvement
- 2028-03-12 09:30 UTC: SRE applied conservative rate-limits; readiness to shift pool if necessary
- 2028-03-12 10:10 UTC: Fallback variant enabled for streaming endpoints (customer-assigned)

Current impact: customer reports reduced errors and improving p95/p99 but still elevated by ~20% over baseline during bursts. Marcus believes a full return to baseline requires routing to larger-instance pool and a runtime heuristic fix for the batch-window adaptation.

Requested approvals: 
- Approve up to $5k USD in account credit for the impacted window if mitigation does not fully restore SLOs.
- Approve a controlled instance-pool migration (ops cost covered by infra).

Attachments: mitigation-plan.pdf, timeline.xlsx (short plan and proposed rollback).

Customer-facing note (for immediate use):
"We understand the disruption caused by elevated tail latency. Our engineers have applied mitigations (early-flush batching, conservative rate-limits, fallback model) and are prepared to move your traffic to a larger-instance pool if needed. We will follow up with an executive summary and, if SLOs are not met, a credit for the impacted window."

Please confirm approval or next steps; Marcus/Aditya can start migration once approved.

—Kimberly
